204.title: Composed diagonal-bit bootstrap: the pricing model that called PR205's banked row, audits the queue, and prices the next ladder of kappa gains
204.body:
Under the retained interfaces of the pinned suppliers, this composes **#200**'s
certified bit supplier with **#193/#194**'s complex word through **#194**'s
unchanged assembly and prices it with **#185**'s finite ordinary leaf:

$$\kappa=\frac{1693287}{2500000000}=6.773148\cdot10^{-4},$$

**+0.1826%** over #197's standing claim and **+0.0639%** over the composition as
#202 published it. Adds `research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/` and one
workflow. The package now does three things: prices this composition, **audits the
banked rows that overtook it**, and **prices the ladder of moves that can still
raise kappa**.

## The banked rows arrived, and this package's model called one exactly

This composition was priced at 15:33 UTC. Its lever model then predicted what
banking this word's 2,200 rank-60 exterior corrections would be worth — a row with
`W_per_vertex = 56402/3`, deficit unchanged at 1,936, no rank-60 child left and
coarse saving `683528191056257/10^18`. Within the half hour that row was built and
opened as #205, which states that exact saving and credits this PR as its target;
#206 prices the same row with PR186's entrance banks, and #207 adds 302
coordinated frame changes on top:

| PR | author | kappa | row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#207** | Dugongue | **6.831904550365e-4** | the banked word after 302 coordinated frame changes; current frontier |
| #205 | rohanarun | 6.83061299399923e-4 | PR200's word with its rank-60 exterior corrections banked — the value modelled here |
| #206 | EcmaXp | 6.830611e-4 | the same row via PR186's entrance banks |
| #202 | chafreaky | 6.768823e-4 | the same composition as this PR with the legacy atom wrapper |
| #197 | evmckinney9 | 6.76080316519385e-4 | packed #187's residuals + #193 complex + the finite leaf |
| this | Maxime Fleury | 6.773148e-4 | #200's bit + #193's complex + #185's finite leaf on #194's assembly |

`audit.py` prices #205's, #206's and #207's rows from byte-identical copies of
their certificates under `references/queue/` and requires each result to appear
**verbatim** in the certificate it came from. All three reproduce to the last
digit, and each sits at its own word's ceiling: with the bit branch binding,
`kappa = C/(1+C)` and there is no pricing room left in any of them.

## New ways to raise kappa, priced

PR184's assembly takes `a = min(bit leaf, (1-1e-9)*C_complex - 1e-10)` and returns
`kappa = a/(1+a)` on the `10^-10` grid, so **the smaller branch is the whole
constraint** and a gain on the stronger side is worth nothing until the other side
catches up. Today the bit branch binds at `6.831904e-4` while the complex side caps
at `7.004273e-4`: **+2.52% is available with no complex-side work at all.**

`targets.py` prices the moves that get there. For a fixed stock and deficit the
coarse saving is `C = (1 - mass/(W m)) / L` with `L` the rank-mass-weighted mean of
`ln(m/r)`, so the lever is `L`: a ledger whose residual dirt sits in fewer, larger
children. Soaking every child of rank at or below a threshold into the largest
admissible child gives, on the queue's own rows:

| soak | bit coarse saving | complex coarse saving | kappa | gain | binds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| today | 136731504666219/2e17 | 350459221139329/5e17 | 6.831904e-4 | — | bit |
| bit only, rank-1 | 792978386838687/10^18 | — | 7.004273e-4 | +2.52% | complex |
| both, rank-1 | 792978386838687/10^18 | 814442339516203/10^18 | 7.923515e-4 | +15.98% | bit |
| both, rank-2 | 898167154125293/10^18 | 918515942111545/10^18 | 8.973611e-4 | +31.35% | bit |
| both, rank-3 | 981391149202381/10^18 | 1041436537175764/10^18 | 9.804289e-4 | +43.51% | bit |
| both, rank-4 | 1015042828910707/10^18 | 1112905588874264/10^18 | 1.014014e-3 | +48.42% | bit |
| both, rank-8 | 1096975618911405/10^18 | 1243672552482743/10^18 | 1.095774e-3 | +60.39% | bit |
| both, rank-16 | 1178908992537918/10^18 | 1367642974340202/10^18 | 1.177521e-3 | +72.36% | bit |
| cheapest ledgers | 1207154248293627/10^18 | 1391081382485139/10^18 | 1.205699e-3 | +76.48% | — |

The cheapest step is smaller than the table suggests. The bit word needs a coarse
saving of `7.009184e-4` to stop binding, and `targets.py` bisects the smallest-child
population to find the least that delivers it: **moving 57/1000 of the mass in the
bit word's rank-1 children into rank-22 children takes its coarse saving to
`7.009717e-4`**, past the complex word, for `kappa = 7.004273e-4` (+2.52%). The whole
population (377,316 rank-1 children, 9.3% of the rank mass) is worth +16% on its own,
and the complex word's own 87,534 rank-1 children (11% of its mass) do the same for
its side, `7.009184e-4` to `8.144423e-4` (+16.2%).

**What has to change is the child inventory, not the packing.** #207's bank proof
settles the packing side itself: its banks tile width 72 exactly with the word's two
residual families (`6 x rank-4 + 2 x rank-24`, or `3 x rank-24`), and it states that
the current word "has exactly the 4/24 residual families and both tile 72 exactly ...
there is no new LP improvement to add". The children the moment actually charges are
the word's own retained children — internal, source, target, center, compensating and
terminal-substitution children — and it is their inventory, set by the weighted
compilation and by the frame schedule, that holds `L` above `ln(m/22)`.


**All of it is MODELLED, NOT CONSTRUCTED**: no ledger is built here, and each rung
is a shape the assembly would price this way, computed from the queue's certified
rows. The calculator is checked two ways — it equals PR184's own `assemble()` on the
vendored pair, and it reproduces #205's and #207's published kappa to within one
grid step — so a rung is a usable target, in the same way the banked row was.

## What the composition itself does

Exactly one operation: **pricing**. #200 certified a strictly stronger bit word —
coarse saving `677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948355e-4` against #189's
`6.68298937775631e-4` — but published it only with its own complex word, where the
complex branch binds. Composed with the source-assisted complex word
(`219037/312500000 = 7.009184e-4`) the bit branch binds, and PR185's wrapper then
removes the `4.33e-7` of slack PR184's legacy leaf leaves below the coarse saving:

| depth | bit leaf | kappa | vs #197 | vs the unbootstrapped composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (legacy wrapper, = #200's and #202's value) | 6.77340866500955e-4 | 6768823/10000000000 = 6.768823e-4 | +0.1186% | — |
| 1 | 6.77773606501196e-4 | 1354629/2000000000 = 6.773145e-4 | +0.1825% | +0.0639% |
| 2, 3, 8 | 6.77773899999987e-4 | **1693287/2500000000 = 6.773148e-4** | **+0.1826%** | +0.0639% |

The priced bit profile has `m = 72`, `W = 20634`, rank deficit 1936 and 34 terminal
sinks; the claim sits **3.37e-11** below the word's own ceiling
`C/(1+C) = 6.7731483368e-4`, under one `10^-10` selection step, with depths 2, 3 and
8 returning the same grid value. The bit profile, the complex word, the 47-constraint
assembly and the leaf recurrence are the suppliers' and #185's; nothing is re-derived.

`levers.py` is the model behind all of this: it solves the paid-moment inequality
exactly over the rationals and checks itself against three published values, all
reproduced **exactly** because it prices with PR200's own enclosure module
(`references/pr200/interval_moment.py`, vendored byte-identically):

| row | W | D | model = published | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR187's word, unpacked | 63,324 | 5,808 | 167724995262213/250000000000000000 = 6.70899981048852e-4 | PR187's certificate |
| PR187's word, banked | 57,824 | 5,808 | 676537710350481/10^18 = 6.76537710350481e-4 | #197's **certified** packed word |
| PR200's word, unpacked | 61,902 | 5,808 | 677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948354561e-4 | #200's certificate |

## Verification

```bash
python3 -B research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/verify.py
```

Runs from the package directory alone with only the standard library, on Python
3.11 and 3.13, and pins every byte against `SOURCE.json`. It checks that the
certificate regenerates exactly; that depth 0 equals #200's and #202's value; that
PR184's grid legacy leaf against #200's published atom wrapper differs by exactly
one grid step at depth 0 and nothing once bootstrapped; that the claim beats #197
and sits inside one grid step of `C/(1+C)`; that the leaf tolls hold in closed form
and the assembly's own minimum margin excludes the next grid point; that three
corruption controls are refused; that the lever model reproduces its three
published references exactly; **that the audit reproduces #205's, #206's and #207's
own certified coarse savings verbatim**; and **that the target ladder reproduces two
published kappa values, stays monotone and never presents itself as a
construction**. A clean Linux clone of the branch passes and leaves the tree
unchanged; the whole harness runs in about seven seconds.

## Scope and limits

* The physical complex and bit words, their frames, sinks and paid moments are the
  suppliers' certified artifacts, vendored byte-identically and **priced, not
  rebuilt or replayed**. This PR does not re-run their checks, including #205's,
  #206's and #207's: it prices the rows they certify.
* The wrapper is PR185's construction, not one built here; the banked rows are
  #205's, #206's and #207's, not built here; every rung of the ladder is a target,
  not a construction.
* Conditional on PR184's finite bridge and closed-form acceptance arithmetic and on
  the retained contracts of the pinned suppliers. The full multiplication theorem
  remains conditional.
* Dependent on unmerged lines (#200's bit supplier, the #193/#194 complex/assembly
  line, and the #205/#206/#207 bank line).
* Not claimed: a new word, a new all-size hypothesis, priority, or the frontier.
  The frontier belongs to the banked rows above.

## Credits

Bit supplier and the #189/#196 lineage: **chafreaky** (#200, #202), whose enclosure
module this PR vendors and prices with. Banked rows: **rohanarun** (#205, and #197's
packing mechanism this PR models), **EcmaXp** (#206), **Dugongue** (#207, with
PR186's entrance banks). Complex word, pricing and assembly: **icekylinx**,
**GPT-6 Astra** and **ikeboy** (#182/#184/#193/#194). Finite ordinary-leaf wrapper
and recurrence: **rohanarun** (#185). Paired-cube frame, balanced prefix and the 47
constraints: **eumemic** (#168 v4), with the RaD (hipotures) balanced transform and
Zhihao Chen's PR23 gates. The descent figure is **sennemmi**'s (#198); the design
ceiling is **DaysSky**'s (#201); the supplier barriers are **huxint**'s (#203).
Prepared by Maxime Fleury with Codebuff assistance; Apache-2.0; predecessor notices
retained in the package `NOTICE.md`.

203.title: Research: structural barriers for kappa = 0.01 (no new exponent)
203.body:
Current paired-cube refinements leave substantial data-interface and copied-center costs in place. This research package proves explicit limits on several such continuations and tests a different small-network construction. **It reports no new multiplication exponent.**

The new statements are:

- Keeping the pinned #193 complex or #187 bit data calls cannot reach kappa=0.01 even if every auxiliary call and all center loss are granted for free: the ordinary-saving ceilings are below 0.008867 and 0.008898.
- A stated odd-dimensional paired-cube family remains below 0.008094 even with arbitrary local data chains and zero auxiliary entropy. The check includes an analytic infinite tail, not only a finite parameter scan.
- For paired triples with p>=5, every nonzero linear combination of coordinate stars has binary source-support span at least h-2. Consequently any factorization through exactly h copied centers costs at least h(h-2); the current stars attain equality. Overcomplete center factors and different center implementations remain open.
- A common triangular flag for every rational frame in the general finite bit contract forces s>=Wm. The argument also covers commuting frames whose common eigenbasis is not rational.
- On all 87 chronological reuses of the balanced Fano model, every completed scalar permutation obtainable from local GL(2,F2) gates is routable. This extends the earlier fixed-terminal test to every auxiliary/data output permutation in this bounded family.

Only a self-contained research package and its workflow are added to main. Inputs from the unmerged supplier PRs are small pinned profiles; reproduction does not fetch or run those suppliers and does not enlarge their validation scope. The proofs state the interface assumptions and exclusions separately. Optional vector-code solver receipts are not used as independently checked impossibility certificates.

Validation passed on a clean checkout based on main 3b6b668:

```sh
python -B -S research/percent-exponent-architecture/verify.py --deep
```

This regenerates the rational ceilings, checks 59,048 nonzero finite center-coefficient controls and sharp examples, runs seven adverse/unit controls, exhausts the 87 scalar/routing cases in C++17, compares the matching algorithm with eight direct full-word enumerations, and independently replays all 16 retained-demand cases with Python. Verification leaves the checkout unchanged. CI repeats the exact package on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

The whole multiplication theorem remains conditional on its inherited analytic, all-size, precision, row and fixed-tape interfaces. The existing construction, supplier certificates and claimed kappa are unchanged.

Credits and source hashes are in the package NOTICE and manifests, including the paired-cube/compiler authors, #193 and #187 suppliers, DaysSky's #192 entropy ceiling, romainhedouin's #183 assembly ceiling, and the repository's earlier Fano investigations. Prepared for huxint with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

## Result

No word on #144's paired-cube design can certify more than

    κ < 2.5592 × 10⁻³        (complex saving a < 2.5657 × 10⁻³),

whatever its circuit, root groups, gauges, reuse pairs, terminal sinks, frames and `p`. For comparison, the selected construction on main certifies κ = 6.618855 × 10⁻⁴, so the ceiling is about 3.87 times that.

## Scope

The design is the paired-cube ports, the identity `K + H + B = I`, the coordinate-star decoder, the `K` step on the source registers and the three-stage shared cores. A word must obey the eight rules of PROOF.md §3.4. They describe #144's word format, as checked by `scripts/paired_cube/verify.py`, the frame-and-reuse layer of #155–#168 and the terminal-sink gate of #168.

**Not covered:**

- **Source-assisted words** (#184, #191, #193, #194). They use the original source registers as controls and reuse registers after exact cancellation, which breaks rules R1, R2 and R7.
- A different decoder, port family or stage structure.
- The bit supplier. The bound is on the complex saving, and κ is also below the bit saving.

## Argument

Write `D = 2v − 3ℓ` for the deficit and `C = Σ n_r·r·ln(m/r)` for the cost of the ledger's children. Every certified saving satisfies `a < D/C` (from `e^x ≥ 1 + x`), and both assemblies on main force `κ < a/(1+a)`. So it is enough to show that every word pays at least `C(p)`.

The floor comes from one structural fact: along any path of a source value from its injection to a target, frames never decrease. Three lemmas follow, for every `p ≥ 7`.

- **Every source enters at its own line.** Its role's register starts at dimension 1 and must climb to the full space.
- **Every source needs two registers that leave its line and stop again before the full space.** One subspace larger than the line misses at least `4(p−3)` of the source's targets.
- **Every target needs two registers at its own hyperplane, or an extra stop of its own register.**

A charging argument adds these to the fixed cost of the data registers. Each ingredient lowers the ceiling:

| Floor | Ceiling on `a` |
|---|---:|
| data registers and star copies only | 6.3627e-3 |
| + one register per source | 4.2121e-3 |
| + a second register per source | 2.9420e-3 |
| + registers at each target's hyperplane | 2.7868e-3 |
| + source roles enter from frame 0 | 2.7653e-3 |
| **+ the `K` itinerary of the source registers** | **2.5657e-3** |

The maximum over `p` is at `p = 13`. Every `p` from 7 to 99 is evaluated exactly, and a tail bound covers `p ≥ 100`.

[PROOF.md](https://github.com/DaysSky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/design-ceiling/research/design-ceiling/PROOF.md) is self-contained: the ledger, the rules, each lemma with its proof, the charging argument and the numbers.

## Verify

    python3 research/design-ceiling/ceiling.py --check     # the ceiling, exact; under a second
    python3 research/design-ceiling/ceiling.py --brute     # counting lemmas at small p; a few seconds
    python3 research/design-ceiling/model_check.py         # the lemmas on #144's word; about 15 seconds

All three use the standard library only and refuse `-O`.

- **`ceiling.py`** evaluates `D/C(p)` in exact rational arithmetic, with every logarithm enclosed between two rationals, and asserts the side conditions of the charging argument at every `p`.
- **`ceiling.py --brute`** enumerates the counting lemmas: over every vector at `p = 7, 8`, and over one vector from each symmetry orbit for `7 ≤ p ≤ 16`. This is a sanity check; the proofs cover every `p ≥ 7`.
- **`model_check.py`** rebuilds the proof's abstraction for the certified #144 word (`p = 12`) with the repository's own producer. It checks that the abstraction lists exactly the certified children, and that every lemma's conclusion holds on that word.

Run before opening:

- All three pass on Python 3.14 and 3.12 (macOS), and again from a clean export of the commit.
- `model_check.py --tree` also passes on a checkout of #168 (`p = 11`, with frame layer, 2,310 reuse pairs and 47 sinks).

Not run: `make verify`, and anything on Linux. The new workflow runs the three commands on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Limits

- **The proofs are by hand.** Nothing is machine-checked beyond the scripts' exact arithmetic and self-tests, and no one else has reviewed them.
- **The rules are a model of the format.** They are stated in PROOF.md §3.4 so they can be checked against the code. The model check confirms the lemmas' conclusions on two certified words; it does not prove that every acceptable word obeys the rules.
- **The ceiling is far from tight.** On #144's and #168's words the floor is 19% and 26% of the certified cost. The proof charges two registers per source; the certified words use about eight auxiliary registers per port.
- **It was not run on main's selected word** (#186), which is stored in its own archive format.

## Related

- #183 (romainhedouin) gives the assembly's acceptance ceiling in closed form. This PR bounds the supplier saving that enters it.
- #192 bounds one fixed word (#168's) over all frame layouts, at 7.010e-4. This PR bounds every word, far less tightly.

## Credits

- icekylinx: the paired-cube design, its compiler and independent checker, shared cores and assembly (#144, #130).
- eumemic: the frame-and-reuse layer and terminal-sink gate (#155–#168).
- jamesyc: the terminal-sink lemma (#166) and birth-read reuse (#124).
- an664: completed-core sharing (#128).
- romainhedouin: the assembly ceiling (#183).

The lemmas, the charging argument and the scripts were prepared by DaysSky, assisted with Claude.

The circuit has 33 additions per cube instead of 27, but the carrier closure admits 12,189 arcs instead of 10,704, so the virtual auxiliary stock falls from 13,372 to 12,877 roles. All modules, fused outputs and schedules of PR168 are retained; the carrier matching, gauge selection, endpoint frame descent, 2,310 compensated handoffs and 44 terminal-output deletions are regenerated for the new graph. **Bit (new, beyond my #189/#196):** a per-cube bit local circuit found by 100 random restarts and three coordinate-descent rounds over the bit circuit options, each candidate priced through the full physical pipeline: $A[0,0]$, $A[0,1]$, $A[2,0]$ and $A[2,1]$ from the two face diagonals, $A[1,\cdot]$ from direction-0 edges, $G[0,1,0]$ from fixed-coordinate differences (edges elsewhere). The bit virtual stock falls from 19,788 to 18,908 roles (modules, L1 association, partner mixing and output merge unchanged). For this graph a fresh carrier matching and gauge selection are regenerated by the retained generator rules, a complete physical layer (7,282 descended operation frames, 1,760 compensated handoffs) is built by our own producer, and 34 face0 terminal sinks are deleted by James Chang's PR166 substitution. Both suppliers and the paid balanced composition are independently certified. Under the retained interfaces, the bound is

$$
T(n)=O\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{166261725903847}{25\cdot10^{16}}
=0.000665046903615388.
$$

Same headline as my #196 (complex-bound); this PR adds the stronger bit supplier. The refined complex profile has 10,523 physical auxiliary roles, 13,163 persistent roles, rank mass 867,438, deficit 1,320 and largest child 20; its saving is $665489485337/10^{15}=0.000665489485337$. The new bit profile has 17,114 physical roles, 20,634 persistent roles, rank mass 1,483,712, deficit 1,936 and largest child 60; its coarse saving is $677773948354561/10^{18}=0.000677773948355$ (PR189: $0.000668298937776$; PR168 v4: $6600253/10^{10}$), and the established atom wrapper gives ordinary saving approximately **0.000677340914792**, 1.42% above the PR189 bit supplier that #194 composes with. With this package's own complex word the complex branch binds, so the headline bound equals #196; the contribution here is the certified bit profile. Composed with the source-assisted complex word of #193/#194 (saving 7.009e-4) it would give about 6.769e-4, which I am preparing as a separate stacked composition with full credit.

The configurable circuit is icekylinx's (PR144); the complex part only selects a different configuration. Carrier arcs come from our own legal-edge Hopcroft–Karp matching on coordinate-padded frames, extended by DaysSky's PR162 rule, and are replayed by the retained `compile_closure` with its acyclicity and span checks. The new bit graph is admitted through the retained package checker (exact rational frames, mod-2 decoder, geometry, chains, partner chronology, F2 replay, ledger and five mutation controls). The physical bit layer follows PR131's descent rule (each frame between the join of its incoming frames and the meet of its outgoing frames) on exact rational subspaces, repaired to nondegenerate bases, with handoffs read at the recipient's first use; the 34 sinks are the face0 roots whose rank-21 caps contain every write, with the complete modified target chronology, all 17,114 dirty columns over F2 and over the integers, and exact prime witnesses for all 24,401 used frames. The same producer applied to PR168's unchanged bit graph reproduces a layer slightly above PR168's own (6.60082e-4 vs 6.60025e-4 coarse before sinks), which is the control for the bit-side pipeline. The exact four-file PR175 overlay at `f1081fabbfadaaaaf7292a40d428dbbb865ce920` is retained in the verification baseline.

No mathematical hypothesis or ordinary-supplier interface is strengthened. General Clifford/tensor, uniform weighted compilation, restored-row, paid-layout, precision/recovery and analytic fixed-tape contracts remain the stated assumptions. The finite certificate is not an unconditional multiplication theorem.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex assistance. The prerequisite construction is eumemic's PR168 v4, retaining its Anthropic Claude/OpenAI Codex disclosures and earlier PR144/161 lineage. 199.title: Bit leaf bootstrap: queue standing + the deferred #200 composition at conditional kappa = 6.773148e-4
199.body:
**Conditional kappa = 267141/400000000 = 6.6785250e-4** (+0.0629% over #194's
1668581/2500000000 = 6.674324e-4).

Self-contained on `main`: the pinned inputs it needs — #194's assembly route, the complex and bit
certificates, and the PR168 v4 pinned export — are vendored byte-identical under
`research/source-assisted*/` and `research/paired-cube-twin-local-168/certificate.json`, so
`verify.py` runs on this branch alone. Those inputs are #194's (and, through it, #193/#189/#185/#184/#182's)
and are not claimed here. Package: `research/bit-leaf-bootstrap-189/`.

## Where we are (2026-10-09)

The queue moved after this PR opened. Exact standing claims, read from the open
pull requests:

| PR | author | kappa | lever | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #200 | chafreaky | 6.65046903615388e-4 | new bit **and** complex supplier | With its own complex word the *complex* branch binds, so the headline equals #196. It states that composed with #193/#194's complex its bit supplier "would give about 6.769e-4, which I am preparing as a separate stacked composition". |
| **#197** | evmckinney9 | **6.76080316519385e-4** | packs #187 rank-4/rank-24 residuals + #193 complex + the finite leaf | **The highest standing kappa claim.** Its body: +0.8398% packing gain. |
| #198 | sennemmi | 6.679123e-4 | 102 lowered #189 endpoint frames + the finite leaf | Draft; explicitly "not claimed as the current public record" and "do not claim to beat #197". Credits this PR: the recurrence "first applied to PR189 by PR199". |
| #199 | this PR | 6.678525e-4 | finite leaf bootstrap on #194's inputs | Reproduces #194's kappa exactly; the leaf is the only change. |

So on #194's inputs this PR's headline is **superseded on the number**: by **#198**
(the same recurrence on a *descended* #189 word) and by **#197** (a stronger bit
word). This PR's first published application of the #185 bootstrap to #189's word
is credited there and is no longer the record; what it still contributes is the
reproduction harness, the two maximality proofs, and a pricing path that composes
the queue's newest supplier — which produces the highest value below.

## Beating the standing best: the composition #200 deferred, plus this leaf

#200 supplies a strictly stronger bit word (coarse
`677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948355e-4` against #189's
`668298937775631/10^18 = 6.68298937775631e-4`) but does *not* publish the stacked
composition; it announces it as separate work. `research/bit-leaf-bootstrap-189/next_bit_composition.py`
prices any certified bit profile through #194's unchanged assembly against
#193's complex, so that deferred composition is now computed, with this PR's
bootstrap applied on top:

| depth | bit leaf | kappa | vs #197 | vs this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (legacy atom wrapper = #200's own "about 6.769e-4") | 6.77340866500955e-4 | 6768823/10000000000 = 6.768823e-4 | +0.1186% | +1.3521% |
| 1 | 6.77773606501196e-4 | 1354629/2000000000 = 6.773145e-4 | +0.1825% | +1.4168% |
| 2, 3 | 6.77773899999865e-4 | **1693287/2500000000 = 6.773148e-4** | **+0.1826%** | +1.4168% |

The depth-0 row independently confirms the harness: #200 says the stacked
composition "would give about 6.769e-4", and this returns 6.768823e-4 from that
supplier's certificate. The bit side still binds at every depth
(6.7777e-4 < 7.0092e-4), so **this is the highest kappa computed anywhere in the
queue** — +0.1826% over the standing claim #197, and +0.0639% over the depth-0
row #200 has announced but not published.

**Pricing headroom is now exhausted on this word.** For a fixed bit word the
assembly caps kappa at `C/(1+C)`; #200's `C = 6777739/10^10` gives
`C/(1+C) = 6.7731483368e-4`, and the depth-2/3 rows sit 3.4e-11 below it. Finer
pricing cannot move the number. Both remaining levers reduce `W` on *that* word,
and both are new work on #200's graph rather than a recomposition:

* **endpoint-frame descent** — what #198 did on #189's word, worth +0.0090% of
  coarse saving there (`6.68298937775631e-4 -> 6.6835882709e-4`).
* **residual packing** — #197's mechanism, bound to #187's word, worth +0.8403%
  of coarse saving (`6.70899981048852e-4 -> 6.76537710350481e-4`) — the largest
  single bit-side gain in the queue.

Because the bit branch binds, complex-side work is worthless until a bit coarse
saving passes the complex's 7.009184e-4.

#200's certificate is vendored byte-identical at
`research/bit-leaf-bootstrap-189/inputs/pr200-bit-certificate.json`, digest pinned
in `SOURCE.json`, and priced — not rebuilt or replayed.

## What changes on #194's own inputs

Exactly one thing in the record: the ordinary leaf that prices the binding bit
supplier. #194 sets `kappa = a/(1+a)` with
`a = min(bit_effective, (1-1e-9)*complex_saving - 1e-10)`, and the bit side binds
(6.6788e-4 versus 7.0092e-4) — but it prices that side with PR184's legacy
ordinary leaf `OLD = 384599/10^10 = 3.84599e-5`, which holds the effective value
4.207e-7 *below* PR189's coarse saving `C = 6.68298937775631e-4`. PR185 replaced
that legacy leaf by a finite acyclic wrapper whose leaf value obeys

    a_{n+1} = (1-C)*C + C*a_n = C - C^n (C - a_0).

Applying that recurrence to PR189's bit word on #194's own unchanged assembly:

| depth | bit leaf | kappa | gain vs #194 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (record) | 6.67878244234e-4 | 1668581/2500000000 | — |
| 1 | 6.68298618876e-4 | 3339261/5000000000 = 6.678522e-4 | +0.0629% |
| 2 | 6.68298899812e-4 | 267141/400000000 = 6.678525e-4 | +0.0629% |
| 3 | 6.68298899999e-4 | 267141/400000000 = 6.678525e-4 | +0.0629% |

## Verification

```bash
python3 -B research/bit-leaf-bootstrap-189/verify.py
```

* Pins every input and package file by SHA-256 (`SOURCE.json`).
* Reproduces #194's kappa **exactly** from #194's own profiles through #194's own
  `select()` and `assemble()`; depth 0 *is* that reproduction, so the delta is the
  leaf alone.
* Re-checks 47 strict constraints and 7 margins at every depth, and the strict paid
  atom and row tolls `a_0 < a_n < C < 1 - a_n`.
* Re-prices the vendored #200 certificate, requires the depth-0 row to equal
  `6768823/10^10` (#200's own announced value), and **requires the best row to beat
  #197's claim** — so the workflow fails if either regresses.
* Regenerates `certificate.json` and the workflow runs the same command followed by
  `git diff --exit-code`.

## Searched and rejected

Both W-lowering levers on #189's bit word are maximal, so that word's leaf slack
was the last room before a new bit word is needed (`word.py::row()` gives
`W = 2*v + (R - pairs)` at fixed rank deficit, so sinks and pairs each raise the
coarse saving):

* **terminal sinks: 34 of 34.** All 474 per-root-admissible sink roots were
  enumerated; the shipped 34 reproduce the frozen profile bit-for-bit, and every one
  of the 440 rank-23 extras is rejected by the exact target chronology of
  `terminal.py::prove` (`target chain nesting`), so no larger target-disjoint packing
  exists.
* **donor reuse: 1760 of 3960 gauges.** Every one of the 2200 unpaired gauges has a
  rank-20 entrance birth frame, and no donor end frame among all 8628 is contained in
  any of them, so no donor can be aliased in (`word.py::exact_frames` eligibility).

A frame-layout search on the same word was started and abandoned: re-choosing
operation frames only moves kappa when chain gaps are re-nested, and #198 published
a deterministic endpoint-frame descent that does this properly (#192 bounds the
family's frame-layout ceiling at 7.010e-4, which the complex side already attains).

Commands and observed output: `research/bit-leaf-bootstrap-189/bit-maximality.md`
(run against #189's package, an open dependency not vendored here).

## Scope and limits

* The physical complex and bit words and their sink/reuse/frame artefacts are
  inherited pinned inputs (#168 v4 `fd25adb7`, #182/#184/#189/#193/#194, #200).
  This PR re-prices the assembly; it does not rebuild or replay the words. The
  wrapper's physical realization is #185's claimed construction, not one built
  here; #200's bit word is that author's certified artifact, vendored and priced.
* Conditional on #183's closed-form acceptance ceiling, #184's finite bridge, and the
  retained contracts of the inputs.
* On #194's inputs the gain is small (0.0629%) and lives on the 10^-10 selection
  grid, where the bootstrapped value saturates at the same kappa the untolled limit
  `C` gives. The #200 composition is larger (+0.1826% over #197) but rests on an
  unmerged supplier and on the same conditional wrapper.

Credits: eumemic (#168 v4), icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra (#182/#184), rohanarun (#185),
chafreaky (#182/#189/#200), ikeboy (#193/#194), romainhedouin (#183), DaysSky (#192),
evmckinney9 (#197), sennemmi (#198). See `NOTICE.md` in the package.

192.title: A κ ceiling of 7.010e-4 for every frame layout of #168's word (no new κ)
192.body:
Adds `research/kappa-ceiling/` and one workflow; **no existing file changes and no new κ.** #168's word is not on main, so the package carries the 48 files of #168 it reads (scripts, frozen frames, pairs, sinks, modules and certificates) as a pinned archive, `baseline-pr168.tar.gz` (0.6 MB). It rebuilds them in a temporary directory, following `research/coordinated-frames-and-entrance-banks`. Each file's sha256 is pinned in `SOURCE.json` to commit `4a3c769`. Reviewers can confirm the pins with `git show 4a3c769:<path> | sha256sum`, or rebuild the archive byte for byte with `git archive --format=tar 4a3c769 <paths> | gzip -n -9`.

## Result

No choice of operation frames for #168's complex word can certify more than

    κ < 7010/10^7 = 7.010e-4.

#168's κ = 6.558894e-4 is 93.6% of that. So every frame refinement still possible on this word is worth at most **+6.9%** in total. Going further needs a different circuit, different reuse or gauges, or a different design.

The ceiling covers one word. Its DAG, operations, carrier arcs, 2,310 gauges and reuse pairs, and 47 terminal sinks stay fixed, and only the operation frames vary. It does not bound constructions that change any of those.

## Argument

Write `D = 2v − 3ℓ` for the shared-core deficit and `C = Σ n_r·r·ln(m/r)` for the cost of the children.

1. **Every certified saving satisfies `a < D/C`.** This follows in two lines from `e^x ≥ 1 + x`. On #168 the certified savings sit within 0.09% of `D/C`.
2. **κ < G(a).** `G` is the assembly's closed-form acceptance ceiling from #183 (romainhedouin), and it is increasing in `a`.
3. **Splitting a frame climb into more steps only costs more,** because `r·ln(m/r)` is subadditive.
4. **No frame layout can push `C` below a floor `C_floor`.** The floor comes from three ingredients:
   - frame bounds propagated jointly through both registers of every operation;
   - an exact per-register dynamic programme over frame dimensions;
   - Lagrangian coupling of the two registers of each operation. Each of the 400 integer rounds is itself a valid floor.

Hence `κ < G(D/C_floor)`. Each stage of the floor lowers the ceiling:

| Floor | Ceiling on κ |
|---|---:|
| two steps per register | 1.153e-3 |
| joint bounds + per-register programme | 7.158e-4 |
| **+ Lagrangian coupling** | **7.010e-4** |

[PROOF.md](https://github.com/DaysSky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/kappa-ceiling-168/research/kappa-ceiling/PROOF.md) has the statements and proofs. It also gives weaker design ceilings for any word with #168's ports and decoder, from 4.08e-3 to 1.25e-2 under stated hypotheses.

## Verify

    python3 research/kappa-ceiling/ceiling.py --check     # stdlib only, about 50 seconds; -O is refused

The script rebuilds the pinned #168 files after checking the archive and every file hash, then regenerates #168's complex word with #168's own producer. It reads the frozen physical layer and terminal sinks, computes every bound and compares the results with `expected.json`. A tampered archive is rejected. `--tree PATH` runs on a full #168 checkout instead. It checks itself:

- #168's own layout lies inside every derived frame bound;
- its slot chains reproduce #168's certified complex ledger child for child, and the sink record;
- every per-slot floor, and every Lagrangian round's total, lies below #168's actual cost.

All bounds use exact integers with rounded-down logarithms, so the printed ceiling is an upper bound.

Run before opening:

- `--check` passes on this branch (Python 3.14, macOS), from the archive alone and on a full #168 checkout.
- On this branch, `research/bit-reuse-147/verify.py`, `research/bit-elim-144/verify.py` and `tests/test_recycled_bit_integration.py` pass. They failed in an earlier version of this PR that carried #168's scripts.

Not run: the full `make verify`. The new workflow runs `--check` on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Scope and limits

- The proofs are elementary but not machine-checked beyond the script's exact arithmetic and self-tests. No one else has reviewed them.
- The ceiling is about #168's word only. Newer PRs (#181 onward) change the word, and each would need its own run. Constructions kept in their own package format, such as #186's, would need an adapter.
- The pins refer to #168 at `4a3c769`. If #168 changes, the archive and `expected.json` stay valid for that commit and would need a new version for the new one.

## Credits

- eumemic: #168, its physical-layer word and checker, and the terminal-sink gate.
- icekylinx: the paired-cube framework, compiler, gauges, shared cores and assembly (#144, #130).
- romainhedouin: the closed-form assembly ceiling (#183).
- jamesyc: the terminal-sink lemma (#166).

The bounds, the frame floor and the script were prepared by DaysSky, assisted with Claude.
